title: Singapore presses US on new AI chip export rules, minister tells Semafor
excerpt: Singapore's Josephine Teo says her government is talking to US officials about new AI chip licence rules, and that its Megaspeed probe continues.
content_html:
Singapore is asking US officials how new rules on AI chip sales will work, minister Josephine Teo said on Monday. She spoke at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event, as Brendan Ruberry reported for Semafor.

Teo, who runs Singapore’s digital ministry, said she had spoken with Christopher Landau, the US deputy secretary of state.

“I think more importantly, how we can facilitate trusted access to this very important AI infrastructure,” Teo said.

The US Commerce Department put out an interim rule on Monday. Firms now need a licence to ship top AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.

The rule also hits data centres abroad that rent US chips to Chinese firms. Singapore-based Megaspeed, the company at the centre of the scandal that ended Jensen Huang’s time as Nvidia’s chief executive, is accused of using that route. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had put off adding Singapore to the list several times, until his department came under fire, Semafor reported.

Teo said Singapore takes the law seriously and is home to about 6,000 US firms. She added that it does not accept firms that break other countries’ laws.

“If they also violate our laws, they can be very certain that we will actively investigate and also hold them to account,” she said.

Teo would not discuss her government’s claim that the US had not helped much with its Megaspeed probe. Last week, Singapore’s home affairs ministry said it had received limited US help. Teo said Singapore began its own probe before it knew of the US one, and that the work goes on.

She also said OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind have expanded in Singapore in recent months. Singapore will try to keep access to the computing power that lawful firms need, she said.
